The residence visa enables living in Sharjah legally. Applicants need to hold a valid residence visa. If your residence visa has expired,  the foremost thing you should know is the residence visa renewal charges in Sharjah for 2025. The regulatory rules for visas are constantly evolving. Being updated with the latest, information means being aware of costs, procedures, and requirements. This will help you get prepared and avoid any fines or delays.

This article encompasses all the details about the renewal of a residence visa in Sharjah. Be aware of costs, documents, timelines, and expert tips to make the process smooth and stress-free.

Understanding the Importance of Residence Visa Renewal

Legally stay or work in the UAE by holding a residence visa. This enables access to essential services in the UAE. The penalties are implied in case of residence visa expiry or deportation may occur in severe cases. 

Who Needs to Renew Their Residence Visa?

  • Employees under company sponsorship
  • Family members under a spouse or parent’s sponsorship
  • Investors and business owners holding an investor visa
  • Retirees and property owners with a residency visa

2025 Updated Residence Visa Renewal Charges in Sharjah

The cost of renewing your visa in Sharjah depends on various factors such as the visa type, duration, and medical examination fees. Below is a general breakdown of the expected expenses:

Visa Type Renewal Fees (AED) Medical Test Fees (AED) Emirates ID Fees (AED)
1-Year Work Visa 2,500 – 4,000 250 – 700 370 – 1,070
2-Year Work Visa 3,500 – 5,500 250 – 700 370 – 1,070
Investor/Partner Visa 4,000 – 6,500 250 – 700 370 – 1,070
Family Visa (Spouse/Child) 3,000 – 5,000 250 – 700 370 – 1,070
Golden Visa (10 Years) Varies 250 – 700 Varies

(Note: These are estimated costs for 2025 and may change based on government regulations.)

Required Documents for Residence Visa Renewal in Sharjah

To avoid any delays, ensure you have all the necessary documents before starting the process. Here’s what you need:

  • Original Passport (valid for at least six months)
  • Current Residence Visa Copy
  • Emirates ID Copy
  • Recent Passport-Sized Photos
  • Tenancy Contract or Ejari (proof of residence in Sharjah)
  • Medical Test Report (mandatory for applicants over 18 years old)
  • Health Insurance (as per UAE regulations)
  • Sponsor’s Documents (for family visa renewal)

Step-by-Step Process for Renewing Your Residence Visa in Sharjah

Follow the right steps and fulfill the requirements timely and accurate. Renewing your residence visa in Sharjah is a simple and trouble-free process. Look at the breakdown:

Step 1: Undergo a Medical Fitness Test

The medical assessment is the foremost and unavoidable step. To do this, visit an authorized medical center in Sharjah. Within 24-48 days, the results will be declared.

Step 2: Apply for Emirates ID Renewal

Apply to obtain your Emirate ID renewal. This is done through the Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship (ICP). These steps come after the medical test.

 This step comes after the medical test.  apply for your Emirates 

Step 3: Submit Your Visa Renewal Application

Your employer, sponsor, or PRO (Public Relations Officer) will handle the submission through Amer Centers or the GDRFA Sharjah online portal.

Step 4: Pay the Required Fees

Submit the required Sharjah residence visa renewal fees timely. The cost varies with the visa category.

Step 5: Wait for Visa Stamping

Your passport will be stamped once the procedure is approved, and your passport will be stamped with the renewed residence visa. This process typically takes 2-5 business days.

Common Reasons for Visa Renewal Delays & How to Avoid Them

The delays might occur even after the proper planning. Take the common possible reasons into account that can disrupt the visa renewal process. Check the key reasons and solutions:

  • Incomplete Applications: Every detail counts when submitting your documents. Double-check all information, ensuring accuracy before submission to avoid rejection.
  • Technical Issues: Online systems sometimes experience downtime. If you’re applying online, check government portals regularly and be prepared to visit an Amer Center if necessary.
  • Employer or Sponsor Delays: If your visa is under company sponsorship, delays on their end can slow your renewal. Regularly follow up with your HR or PRO to keep the process moving.
  • Payment Issues: Missing or incorrect payments can cause processing delays. Ensure all Sharjah residence visa renewal fees are paid correctly and request confirmation receipts.

Recognize these steps early and address them timely. This leads to a reduced possibility of experiencing unwanted setbacks and makes obtaining your visa renewal easier.

What Happens if You Don’t Renew Your Residence Visa on Time?

In case of residence visa expiry and failure to renew it, penalties will be imposed on visa holders.

  • Overstay Fines: AED 50 per day after the grace period
  • Travel Restrictions: You may not be able to exit the country without paying fines
  • Legal Consequences: In extreme cases, authorities may take legal action or impose additional penalties

Tips for a Smooth Residence Visa Renewal Process

A successful visa renewal requires careful planning and awareness of the required steps. Follow these expert tips to avoid issues and complete your renewal effortlessly:

  1. Monitor Your Visa Expiry Date Closely: Keep track of your visa’s expiry and initiate the renewal process early to avoid last-minute complications.
  2. Ensure All Documents Are Updated: Expired passports or missing paperwork can halt your application. Keep everything current and in order.
  3. Use Trusted PRO Services for Faster Processing: If you are unfamiliar with the process, professional service providers can assist in ensuring everything is filed correctly.
  4. Check for Any Rule Changes Before Applying: Regulations sometimes change, so confirm the latest updates on the renewal of residence visas in Sharjah through official government websites.
  5. Stay Informed About Processing Times: Some visa types take longer to renew than others. Understand the typical duration and plan accordingly to avoid disruptions.

Taking these proactive steps will help you renew your visa smoothly, ensuring a seamless continuation of your legal stay in the UAE.

Conclusion

The residence visa must stay valid for seamless living in Sharjah. For this, you can renew your visa if it reaches its expiry date. Understanding the residence visa renewal charges in Sharjah helps you plan better and move forward without complications. The protocol includes meeting deadlines, compiling documents early, and keeping a check on any new policy updates, 

However, it is advisable to get an expert consultation. The professionals guide the secure and efficient process of renewing your residence visa. A smooth renewal procedure guarantees continued accessing the benefits of living in Sharjah. Benefits. You can now renew your visa for work, family, or investment purposes in Sharjah.

If you’re confused about the process, get accurate details from the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs GDRFA. If your visa renewal is coming up, don’t wait until the last minute. Start preparing today and ensure a hassle-free experience!

FAQs

How many days does a residence visa renewal take in Sharjah?

Residence visa renewal in Sharjah usually takes around 3 to 5 working days once all documents are submitted and approved by immigration. Delays may occur if medical or Emirates ID processing takes longer.

How can I renew my UAE residence visa in Sharjah?

To renew your visa, complete a medical fitness test, renew your Emirates ID, and submit your application through the GDRFA Sharjah office or online portal. After paying the renewal fees and uploading documents, your visa will be stamped in your passport once approved.

What documents are required for a residence visa renewal in Sharjah?

You’ll need a valid passport, current residence visa, recent passport-size photo, medical fitness certificate, Emirates ID copy, proof of accommodation (Ejari or tenancy contract), health insurance, and your sponsor’s documents if you are under family sponsorship.

What is the cost for a family visa renewal in Sharjah?

The cost for renewing a family residence visa in Sharjah generally ranges from AED 3,000 to AED 5,000. This includes visa processing, Emirates ID renewal, and medical test fees, though the total may vary based on visa type and service provider.

Can I renew my Sharjah residence visa online?

Yes, you can renew your residence visa online through the UAEICP or GDRFA Sharjah portals. The process allows you to upload required documents, pay fees, and receive approval digitally, making it faster and more convenient than visiting the immigration office.
